name: Prince of Greece
overview: The Prince of Greece is a male figure mentioned in the book of Daniel, described as an angelic being who was about to arrive after the angel Michael delivered his message to Daniel. His tribal affiliation is not specified. The nature of this figure suggests a spiritual or angelic role rather than a human one.
namesAndTitles: The title 'Prince of Greece' means 'prince of Javan,' which is the Hebrew term for Greece. This title is not a personal name given by God but rather a designation indicating his association with the region of Greece, as referenced in Daniel 10:20.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the Prince of Greece beyond what is indicated by his title and unique attribute. No additional relationships are listed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The Prince of Greece holds significance in the biblical narrative as a spiritual being involved in the heavenly conflict described in Daniel. His impending arrival after Michael's message to Daniel highlights the ongoing spiritual battles related to earthly kingdoms, emphasizing God's sovereign control over nations through angelic agents. This figure underscores the reality of unseen spiritual forces influencing historical events in accordance with God's purposes.
